request.deadline: 18 months, with milestones from Q3 2026 through 2027
deliverables: Establish a not-for-profit entity or host-organization agreement and publish a technical transition architecture and migration plan in Q3 2026.
Launch a public usage dashboard in Q3 2026.
Hold a board election via on-chain voting under published rules in Q4 2026.
Serve all public API traffic for mainnet, preview, and preprod from the new stack in Q1 2027.
Transfer Blockfrost source code, trademarks, domain names, and associated assets to the governing entity in Q1 2027.
Open a public sustainability consultation and publish a long-term sustainability proposal in Q2-Q3 2027.
Operate the public API at a minimum 99% monthly uptime SLA and publish quarterly technical and budget reports during 2027.
request.what: Fund an 18-month transition and operation of Blockfrost as a free, community-governed not-for-profit public API for Cardano.

claims.claim: Blockfrost is presented as a reliable hosted REST interface that lets developers interact with Cardano without running their own node infrastructure.
The proposal states that Blockfrost usage in the Cardano Foundation developer ecosystem survey rose from 39.3% in 2022 to 71.5% in 2025, with links to the survey pages.
The proposal states that Blockfrost served 781k unique visitors, more than 1.84 billion API requests, almost 700 requests per second, and over 7 TB of API data last month.
The proposal states that in most Cardano epochs more than 50% of all transactions are submitted through Blockfrost.
The proposal states that more than 100 Icebreakers have joined the effort to decentralize Blockfrost operations.
The proposal requests 9,832,979 ADA, equivalent to 1,868,266 USD at 0.19 USD per ADA, for 18 months of transition and operations.
The budget allocates 7,780,347 ADA to staffing, 1,894,737 ADA to operations and infrastructure, and 157,895 ADA to legal and accounting.
The proposal says all Blockfrost intellectual property, including source code, trademarks, domain names, and associated assets, will be transferred to the governing not-for-profit entity.
The proposed governance model includes a five-seat board, with four seats for open-source infrastructure development entities and one community seat, preceded by a named preliminary board.

The proposal states that future sustainability may come from not-for-profit commercial paid tiers or a vendor-backed model, with profits, membership fees, revenue, and costs intended to support the free public API and reduce future treasury dependence.

summary: The document requests 9,832,979 ADA for an 18-month transition of Blockfrost into a community-governed not-for-profit public API, with staged governance, service migration, IP transfer, reporting, and uptime deliverables, but several key usage, decentralization, and sustainability claims are asserted without direct evidence in the document.
